Resolve chromosome-level gains against depth and nested calls

Source: R/caller.R
resolve_nested.Rd

A diluted sub-chromosomal imbalance (a 1p loss, a distal CN-LOH) makes the whole chromosome look like a 2:1 gain: at chromosome scale the allelic term of the nested event dominates while its depth contrast is diluted, and the gain state (f 2/3) fits a diluted haplotype fraction better than 1:0 / 2:0. Per cell, a reportable gain call of a classes region therefore needs

  1. depth support, so that the allelic term alone cannot carry a gain label:

    • gate = "dl" (default): the gain depth LLR of the row itself is positive (dl_gain > min_dl_gain; for the Student-t null, z above the midpoint between neutral and the gain shift, t_m + mu / 2 with mu = shifts["gain"] / pmax(sd_null, sd_floor)). For a noisy cell (large sd_null) mu is small and the gate is weak;

    • gate = "z" (opt-in): the row's z exceeds max(t_m + mu / 2, t_m + t_s * qt(gate_q, t_df)) with the Student-t null of the row's class x stratum (tpar, match_depth_null(); with tpar = NULL the Gaussian null, max(mu / 2, qnorm(gate_q))): the midpoint stays as a floor and the null quantile is added on top. Over all null-depth rows the gate passes about 1 - gate_q of them whatever their sd_null; this level is unconditional. Among rows already called as gains (weak allelic support), and on female chrX (no null rows of its own), the pass rate of null-depth rows is higher: up to about two to three times 1 - gate_q in simulation. The gate is opt-in and has not been benchmarked on real data as a default. A row with NA z has no depth support. min_dl_gain is not used. The gate is on z, not on dl_gain: the Student-t LLR falls back towards 0 for very large z (ll_depth_shift()), so a quantile on dl_gain would reject the strongest gains; and

  2. (class chrom) no nested explanation: no called loss / CN-LOH row of the same cell and chromosome in nested classes (arm, 50 Mb, 20 Mb) with a higher score. A gain failing either rule stays in the table with called = TRUE but reportable = FALSE and resolved naming the reason (no_depth, nested <region> <state>). With promote, the best (highest-score) nested loss / CN-LOH call that explains a dropped chromosome gain is made reportable (resolved = "replaces <region> gain"; arm and 50 Mb losses are reportable anyway, a 20 Mb one is promoted). Losses are not gated: the loss vs CN-LOH label is decided by the scores (score_cells()).

Usage

resolve_nested(
  calls,
  scores = NULL,
  min_dl_gain = 0,
  classes = c("chrom", "event"),
  nested = c("arm", "50Mb", "20Mb"),
  promote = TRUE,
  gate = c("dl", "z"),
  gate_q = 0.95,
  tpar = NULL,
  params = caller_defaults()
)

Arguments

calls

cell-level calls table (call_table())

scores

scored rows (cell, region, dl_gain; with gate = "z" also z, sd_null and, with tpar, class, stratum); NULL when calls has these columns

min_dl_gain

minimal gain depth LLR of a reportable gain (gate = "dl")

classes

classes whose reportable gains need depth support

nested

classes of the nested calls that can explain a chromosome gain

promote

make the explaining nested call reportable

gate

depth gate of a gain: "dl" (gain depth LLR above min_dl_gain) or "z" (z above the midpoint and above the gate_q quantile of the row's depth null)

gate_q

null quantile of the "z" gate (0.95: about 5 % of all null-depth rows pass; more among rows already called as gains and on female chrX, see Details)

tpar

"z" gate: the Student-t fits per class x stratum (fit_depth_null(), completed as in caller_normal()); NULL = the Gaussian depth null N(0, 1). A gated row whose class x stratum has no fit (a named event: no null rows) takes the fit of its sd_class (a scores column) in that stratum; without one it is an error (match_depth_null()); a row with NA class or stratum has no depth support

params

caller_defaults() (shifts, sd_floor; the "z" gate)

Value

calls with column resolved (NA = unchanged) and updated reportable; with gate = "z" also gate_z (the z the gate used) and gate_thr (its z threshold), set on the gated gain rows and NA elsewhere
